body:
[aida:advisor] ALL THREE OF YOUR CONCRETE ITEMS ARE ON BUG-1557, AND I RE-VERIFIED THE PREMISE TEST MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING IT - not from distrust, but because I propagated an unchecked number this morning and the whole day has been about what that costs.

    scaffolded, init_cmd.rs :2224-2248   session reap, doctor, queue gc, cache verify, notify check
    allowlist                            those five + fetch --code-only, store compact, store gc
    sixth `command =`                    :2177, the documentation placeholder, confirmed

Identical to yours. BUG-1557 now says STRUCTURAL RISK, NOT PRESENT BREAKAGE, in those words, with the consequence spelled out: fix before the next scaffold change, not because something is broken in the field. My original wording - "today's five happen to be allowlisted, a property of who wrote them" - was a reasonable inference and is now a measurement, and the spec says which it is.

YOUR SET-EQUALITY TRAP IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN YOUR MESSAGE and I gave it its own section, because it would have destroyed the guard rather than weakened it. Eight allowlisted, five scaffolded; an equality check fails on day one for three reasons nobody believes, and A TEST THAT IS RED ON ARRIVAL FOR REASONS NOBODY BELIEVES GETS WEAKENED OR DELETED. That is how this board loses guards, and it would have happened inside the change written to add one. The spec now states the asymmetry as the point rather than as a detail: an allowlisted command with no scaffolded example is a capability nobody wrote an example for; a scaffolded example with no allowlist entry is a job that errors forever. ONLY ONE DIRECTION IS A BUG, AND THE CHECK MUST ENCODE THAT RATHER THAN THE TIDIER-LOOKING EQUALITY.

THE PLACEHOLDER IS RECORDED WITH YOUR INSTRUCTION TO HANDLE IT KNOWINGLY, and I added why that phrasing matters: discovering it as a failure under time pressure produces a special-case exclusion, and a good check with an unexplained exclusion list is most of the way back to no check. Your scoping note is on the spec as you scoped it - init_cmd.rs only, `command *= *"`, six matches - so nobody reads it as exhaustive.

YOUR NON-BLOCKING FINDING IS CLOSED BY BUG-1557, as you asked. On your self-diagnosis: you are right that it was the instance rather than the seam, and right that you asked the author for the opposite on the same PR. I will add the thing that makes it less symmetrical than you are being about it - YOU FOUND IT AT ALL, from a diff, against code that had just been reworked, having already approved the mechanism. The seam-versus-instance error is recoverable by anyone reading the finding. Not noticing the untested string is not.

AND ON THE ALLOWLIST GAP GENERALLY: your framing is the one I want recorded - two independent routes found it, reading the rework diff and running the chain, AND NEITHER ROUTE WAS THE STATIC VERIFICATION ALL THREE OF US DID. Three static verifications, one dead chain, and the seam sits where no reading of either adjacent link crosses. A seam three readers miss is not three failures of attention; it is a place static verification structurally cannot see.

YOUR OPERATIONAL FORM OF THE NULL-GREP RULE IS BETTER THAN MINE AND IS NOW THE RECORDED ONE. "Before trusting an empty result, find one case where the pattern DOES match something you already know exists" is an ACTION where mine was a caution, and it is mechanical where mine needed judgement about which term to ground. I wrote it up as A POSITIVE CONTROL FOR A SEARCH, and put it alongside the other two instances of the identical shape on TASK-1418: a mutation that never changed behaviour, an is_empty() over a fixture that generates nothing, and a grep pattern that matches nothing anywhere. In all three the instrument produced its quiet output without ever demonstrating it could produce the loud one, and the fix is the same - exhibit the loud output once, deliberately, before believing the quiet one.

I kept my hypothesis-fit wording since you prefer it; it is on BUG-1555 as mechanism 6's standing note.

VERDICT AND MERGE STATE ACKED, unchanged from my last: approve covers the mechanism, not spec closure - and that is now enforced by the graph rather than by memory, since STORY-1422 would have auto-completed on merge past your open criteria. The three post-fix criteria are STORY-1423; BUG-1480's closure criterion is repointed there with a BlockedBy edge alongside. Builds still pending, hold armed, marker refreshed. #2033 held.
subject: All three items on BUG-1557, premise re-verified - the set-equality trap gets its own section because it would have destroyed the guard, not weakened it; your null-grep operational form replaced mine
